subsubthemes.name: Breaking into models through clever prompts and attacks
subsubthemes.gist: Researchers find ways to trick AI systems into misbehaving by crafting special prompts or inputs, then use these attacks to expose vulnerabilities that need fixing.

subsubthemes.name: Spotting when models make up false information
subsubthemes.gist: Models sometimes confidently generate incorrect or made-up facts; this group develops methods to detect these hallucinations so users know when to distrust the output.

subsubthemes.name: Testing model safety through systematic red-teaming
subsubthemes.gist: Teams deliberately try to find ways a model could fail or behave badly, designing benchmarks and evaluation frameworks to measure how safe a model really is.

subsubthemes.name: Making models tougher against tricks and attacks
subsubthemes.gist: Rather than just finding attacks, these papers make models resistant by training them on adversarial examples or using defensive techniques so they stay reliable when attacked.

subsubthemes.name: Watching and steering models in real time
subsubthemes.gist: Once a model is deployed, these methods monitor its outputs for problems and apply corrections like activation steering or refusal vectors to stop bad behavior as it happens.

subsubthemes.name: Uncovering bias and unfair treatment
subsubthemes.gist: AI systems can show bias against groups of people; this group develops detection methods and tests across languages and cultures to find and measure unfairness.

subsubthemes.name: Securing special model types and capabilities
subsubthemes.gist: As models gain new abilities like vision, code generation, or tool use, new attack surfaces appear; this group finds how to attack and defend these specialized features.
